title: What's new in v2.11.0
summary: Change Control: see who changed what and what it did, roll any change back, and roll out the config you got right to your other sites.

steps.title: Change Control
steps.listLabel: See every config change, who made it, and whether it made things worse
steps.body:
Every change on your sites is recorded as it happens: who made it (an admin, Network Optimizer, or UniFi on its own), which fields moved, and what it did to your Security Audit and Site Health. Open one to **Roll Back**.

Site Health before and after a change is compared with what's usual for those hours, with your ISP's part left out, so a drop points at the change and raises an alert.

steps.title: Snapshots
steps.listLabel: Backups of your UniFi Network config, kept off the Console
steps.body: A snapshot is taken on every change and once a day, and kept outside your UniFi Console. **Compare** two, or one against live, to see the Security Audit impact first and then every field that differs. Copies of UniFi's own .unf backups are kept here too.

steps.title: Templates
steps.listLabel: Get a site's networks, Wi-Fi, and firewall right once, then roll them out to the rest
steps.body: Save part of a site's config (networks, Wi-Fi, firewall) as a template. Apply it to another site or a brand new one, or make it a site's **Baseline** so drift from it is flagged. Applying a template creates and updates, never deletes.

steps.title: Config Editor
steps.listLabel: Edit any site's config in one place, and see the Security Audit impact before it's applied
steps.body: Edit every config collection in UniFi's own field names, with completion from this site's networks and zones and problems shown as you type. **Review Plan** shows the Security Audit impact first, and a change that knocks a device offline reverts on its own.

steps.title: Migrate / Restore
steps.listLabel: Replace a device with a different model, re-address your networks, or move to firewall zones
steps.body:
**Replace Device** moves a device's config to new hardware, a different model included: it maps each port with its config (uplink and LAG first), fits AP radio settings to the new model, and gives you a **Re-cabling Sheet** to work from. Once the plan is confirmed, **Forget Old Device** removes the old one.

**Re-address Networks** moves networks to new subnets along with every address in them, and **Set Up Zones** groups them into firewall zones by trust.

steps.title: Site Health
steps.listLabel: One score per site for how good service was, and what hurt it
steps.body: Site Health is the share of user-time with good service across internet, devices, Wi-Fi, and LAN. Each site shows it here worst first, with its top issue. **More** adds the last 24 hours, and each site's Incidents and Changes counts open its list.
